newsitem.title: UK: Queen Elizabeth praises Weizman's peace efforts.
newsitem.headline: Queen Elizabeth praises Weizman's peace efforts.

text.p: Britain's Queen Elizabeth on Tuesday praised Israeli President Ezer Weizman's personal contributions to the quest for peace in the Middle East and reaffirmed the close ties between the two nations.
At a lavish Buckingham Palace dinner to mark the first state visit to Britain of an Israeli president in its 49-year history, the queen said their countrys' pasts have been closely intertwined.
"The past has formed a firm foundation on which a close and vital relationship has been built. Co-operation flourishes everywhere," she said after welcoming him with the traditional toast, Lechayim.

She stressed the strength of the trade links between Britain and Israel, as well as the exchange of ideas and experience in the arts, sciences and technology and offered Britain's hope for a lasting peace in the Middle East.
Her remarks followed clashes on Tuesday between Israeli undercover soldiers and Palestinians in a West Bank village. One person was killed and three others were wounded.

"We pray for a successful conclusion to the negotiation. As president, your personal contribution to the quest for peace has been unstinting, steadfast and greatly admired by your British friends," she said.

"We, in this country, look forward to a day, not far off we hope, when to the relief and satisfaction of all the world, lasting piece will ensure security and justice for the peoples of the region." It was fitting end to the first day of the three-day state visit that began when Weizman and his British-born wife Reuma were given a full ceremonial arrival with a carriage procession to Buckingham Palace.
After a private lunch with the queen and the Duke of Edinburgh and other members of the Royal Family, Weizman visited Westminster Abbbey and laid a wreath at the tomb of the unknown Soldier.
The couple also met members of the Jewish community in London and later took tea with the Queen Mother.

Weizman, who was invited to Britain by the queen, had said he wanted his visit to stress Israel's place in the new world order. The trip also brought back memories of his days as a fighter pilot for the Royal Air Force in World War Two.

Wednesday's itinerary will be just as full. Weizman will meet Prime Minister John Major and the leaders of the opposition Labour and Liberal Democratic parties before visiting London's financial district.

Before departing on Thursday, the president meets United Nations Secretary General Kofi Annan who is also in London, visits a Cambridge University library, tours an RAF base and will contribute to a Holocaust exhibit in London.
